items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: The interviewee (Bill Challis) does not mention Willie Hall in his own turns. The mention of Willie Hall occurs in the interviewer's prose summary/context ('he was using Willie Hall out there'), and the interviewee does not respond to or elaborate on this specific connection.

ctx.x: done with them. There had been no records made or anything like that. He used them because he liked them.

The rest was stage stuff, you know, you come on with "Rhapsody in Blue," and then I think they did part of something of -- I think they did the Rhapsody in Blue, a piece of cut, you know, and they did that, and then the -- Willie Hall had a spot and the Rhythm Boys had a spot, 20 minutes or so, and then they did "Chloe" and then at the end it was "1812 Overture".

Now, you can get awfully sick, if you're in the band, you got to play that stuff, especially when you got some guys that love to improvise, like Jimmy and Tommy and Steve and well, let's see, at that time Trumbauer and Bix had joined, they joined in Indianapolis.
